_comment: Deterministic verb table for the kitchen-sink socket `do:` verbs, generated by reading rust/ws-rs/src/app/host.rs `do_host_action` (every strip_prefix prefix, every explicit match arm, the board: starts_with guard), `needs_window`, and the registry test tables (register_test_do callers: notes:state, compare:*, screenshot:*). One entry per verb or prefix. `headless` class: ok = runs headless (happy returns state, no error); refused = refused with '<action> unavailable in headless mode' and no state change; error = the well-formed happy call itself errors headless. `expect` is a map of dotted paths into the returned state JSON (e.g. 'views.notes.shown'). Only assert what the code really sets headless.

ignore.reason: nested rest.strip_prefix inside the compare: handler (compare:open-sub:<l>|<r>)
nested v.strip_prefix inside the pane: handler (pane:focus:<id>)
nested starts_with inside the paths: handler (paths:select:N)
paths: sub-command (paths:return), not a standalone verb
on|off value of esc-hides: / hide-on-focus-loss:, not a standalone verb
on|off value of esc-hides: / hide-on-focus-loss:, not a standalone verb

verbs.grammar: show:<view> (same set as open:; alias of open)

verbs.note: card views return no error and change nothing headless (the rebuild is a UI-only refresh)
model sub-verbs without a session are no-ops (no error). compare:open:/compare:open-sub:/compare:back are host-level and covered by their own entries.
headless trigger has no main-thread screen list, so no overlay is ever created (shown stays false); the raw screenshot/pane-shot capture verbs are refused separately.
pane:focus:<bogus> errors 'no such pane' (no panes registered headless); pane:<dir> before any view errors 'no view shown'.
record-only: the spec is stored in last_key and exposed in state as top-level `lastKey`; an empty spec is an error instead of a silent no-op.
paths:show is refused headless (needs_window); paths:select:N is out of range while there are no rows — both have their own entries.
needs_window refuses every tool:<panel> headless; the 'not a tool panel' error is only reachable with a real window.

verbs.grammar: tool-close:<panel> (same set tool: accepts, incl. paths)
verbs.note: a bogus or empty panel name is an error ({"error": "not a tool panel: <name>"}) instead of a silent no-op; tool-close:paths maps to paths:hide.

verbs.grammar: board:<sub> (any sub — the Swift jira board verbs are not ported)
verbs.bad_note: every board:* form returns the same not-implemented error, so a distinct bad argument adds nothing
verbs.bad_error: not implemented in the Rust port yet

verbs.grammar: cycle (no argument; two-view toggle Notes <-> Files)
verbs.note: from jira (home) cycle opens files, then notes. It is a two-view toggle: the direction argument is ignored. cycle-back is identical by design — Swift's SharedWindow.cycle(_:) ignores dir too (current == .files ? navNotes : navFiles).

verbs.grammar: cycle-back (no argument; two-view toggle Notes <-> Files)
verbs.note: identical to cycle by design (the -1 direction is ignored in Swift and the Rust port); the two views are Files <-> Notes.

verbs.grammar: back (no argument; returns to the previous view in the bounded history)
show (no argument; opens the last-presented view, else jira)
verbs.note: after the do:home reset, last == jira, so show re-opens jira.
headless counts as 'user already in it', so toggle hides the shown view.

verbs.grammar: switcher-hide (no argument; hide the Ctrl+B W switcher)
verbs.note: a hide/close verb is accepted headless (no-op); the switcher can never be shown headless.

with [jira] already enabled it logs and opens jira. With [jira] disabled, a headless daemon re-enables directly (persists enabled=true and updates state), so it undoes jira-poll-off even without a UI queue.

first call disables [jira] (writes enabled=false to the sandbox commands.toml), reloads, and hides jira. State-dependent: a second call is a no-op. The sandbox is reset in setUpClass so this row sees a fresh enabled=true config.
queues the setup window command; with no ui queue (headless) it is a no-op.
registry hook replies {"available": true} directly, not the full state document — so expect checks the reply dict, not state.

verbs.bad_note: no argument; refusal happens before argument parsing
malformed select (paths:select:bogus) errors 'paths:select:N' — a different message — so it is noted here rather than asserted
verbs.note: headless never has rows, so every well-formed select is out of range.

verbs.grammar: compare:open:<left>|<right> (host-level; opens a compare session; both paths must exist)
verbs.note:
a path that does not exist errors ({"error": "compare: no such path:

"}) and opens nothing; an empty/missing side still opens a (start-page) session.

verbs.grammar: compare:open-sub:<left>|<right> (host-level; opens the compareText sub-view; both paths must exist)
verbs.note: same existence check as compare:open:; a missing path errors and opens nothing.
